title: InferOps inference operations dashboard, v1alpha1
description: The operational dashboard for one InferOps release, as data: the questions an operator asks in the first thirty seconds, the panel that answers each, the PromQL every panel runs, and what the panel shows when there is no number to show. Every expression is held to the correlation query policy in tools/telemetry_correlation and evaluated against the committed synthetic scenarios. The Grafana dashboard JSON under deploy/grafana/ is generated from this file and compared against it. One Grafana has imported it and one real Prometheus has evaluated every panel expression, on one provider, in the states the realRunEvidenceRef record names.

verificationStatus.note: Every panel expression is parsed by the declared PromQL subset, refused if it names a label the catalog bars or nothing carries, reads a series nothing produces, or claims an answer a signal nothing emits cannot give, and evaluated over the six committed synthetic scenarios. Nineteen of the thirty expressions here are accepted correlation queries, repeated verbatim; the other eleven are new in this record. All thirty have since been asked of a real Prometheus, the collector one single-replica release installed on docker-desktop, in nine controlled states, and the generated JSON was imported into one Grafana and rendered in each of six of them. That is one provider, one host, one release, and one Grafana version: not kind, not two replicas, and not Grafana's own schema validation.

dataSource.statement: One data source is one release's collector. The collector the chart installs is release-scoped, so selecting it selects the release; the dashboard carries no namespace or job variable and no expression names a job.
dataSource.notSupported: A store holding two releases' series at once. The chart's recording rules name their own release's jobs, but a panel such as the requests count sums every API series in the store, and would add two releases together.

renderer.statement: The format a dashboard is written in, not a service this project runs. ADR 0004 D7 was amended to make the definition a repository artifact; a Grafana server, who runs it, and where it is exposed remain undecided under telemetry-backend.

states.meaning: A number, and the number is 0. A zero-filled expression is only ever published by a panel that declares zeroMeans, and each fills its zero from something that proves a reading happened: a since-start count only while an API process is publishing its identity, and a share only where requests have been counted. A zero says something was read and counted nothing, never that nothing was read. Zero fills are counts, not rates, because a counter series first appears at whatever it counted before its first scrape and a rate cannot see those events.
states.howShown: The value 0, in the panel's unit.

states.meaning: The panel's expression returned no series. That is a scrape that found nothing, a collector not running, a recording rule not evaluated, or a window with nothing in it, and the panel says which of those its expression can mean.
states.howShown: The panel's whenMissing text, which Grafana shows as its no-value text. It is never a number and a test refuses one that could be read as one.

states.meaning: The panel reads a metric the telemetry catalog declares and marks not emitted. Waiting changes nothing, because no component puts the series on any endpoint.
states.howShown: The title carries 'not emitted', and the panel's whenMissing text names the emitter that is not instrumented.

states.meaning: No series exists that could answer the question in the accepted telemetry, so no expression is published for it.
states.howShown: A text panel whose title carries 'not answerable', stating what would have to exist first. It has no query, so it cannot be mistaken for an empty one.

signals.meaning: An operational figure read from a series the accepted telemetry emits.

Whether the collector reached a target. It is not readiness and not health: the recovery run recorded a deleted serving pod still reading up for fifteen seconds, and a target that is up can be serving nothing. A panel reading up or an inferops:scrape_ recorded series must carry this signal, and its title may not use a word from the checker's readiness and health list -- which is a list, and misses a synonym it was not given.
The panel exists to show that a specified signal is absent.
The panel exists to show that a question has no source.

questions.question: Is this release's collector reaching anything, before any number below is read?
Is the API, the serving runtime, and the model ready?
What traffic and concurrency are observable?
What P50, P95, P99, and throughput can be derived from emitted metrics?
What model-load and recovery signals are emitted?
What CPU, memory, and replica state exist?
Which model, runtime, workload, environment, and provider is running?

panels.title: Scrape targets answering, by tier
panels.description: The fraction of each tier's discovered targets that answered the last scrape. It says the collector reached a process, and nothing about whether that process can serve: a deleted pod has been observed reading up for fifteen seconds after deletion. A tier whose job discovered no pod has no row here rather than a 0: the absence panel beside it is what says so.
panels.whenMissing: Missing: no target was discovered for any tier, or no collector is evaluating this release's recording rules. Every other panel is missing too until this one reads.

panels.title: Scrape jobs that discovered no pod
panels.description: A job whose selector matched no pod publishes no up series at all, so it is invisible in the panel beside this one. These read 1 in exactly that case.
panels.whenMissing: No absence recorded: each job this profile renders has at least one target.

panels.title: API identity not published
panels.description: Reads 1 whenever no API process in this release's namespace publishes inferops_build_info. That is a target answering without one, but it is also every API target down and a job that discovered nothing, because the recorded absence does not read up: read it beside the two scrape panels. The accepted query this repeats is named for the first case only, and that name says more than the expression does. While it reads 1, the since-start counts show missing rather than zero.
panels.whenMissing: No absence recorded: an API process in this release published its identity.

panels.title: Readiness checks failed since the API processes started
panels.description: The API's own readiness refusals, counted since each API process that is publishing now started, summed across replicas: the only readiness signal the platform emits. A count rather than a rate, because a rate cannot see the first refusal of a new component -- the recovery run's single refusal would have read 0 per second. A restarted process starts its count again.
panels.whenMissing: Missing: no API process is publishing its identity right now, so there is nothing to count against. See the collection row. This is not a zero.
panels.zeroMeans: An API process is publishing its identity right now, and no publishing API process has counted a failed readiness check since it started.

panels.title: Readiness checks failed, by component
panels.description: Which readiness component the API names when it refuses traffic: api or serving-adapter. inferops_component is not k8s_component, which is the workload tier. A labelled counter series is created by its first event and first appears at whatever it has counted by its first scrape, at least 1. A rate needs two samples in its window and assumes no zero at creation, so it never sees those events, and for one scrape interval the new series has no row at all. Three refusals counted during startup have been observed beside this rate reading 0. A series that exists and has not moved draws a flat 0 rather than this panel's missing text.
panels.whenMissing: Missing: no readiness check has failed since the API process started, so no series exists, or no API target is scraped. The since-start count separates the two.

panels.title: Model readiness (not emitted)
panels.description: inferops_model_ready is specified, assigned to the serving-runtime adapter, and emitted by nothing. The recorded absence reads 1 to say so rather than leaving an empty panel that reads as a ready model.
panels.whenMissing: Not emitted: the serving-runtime adapter that owns inferops_model_ready is not instrumented, and no collector is evaluating the recorded absence either.

panels.title: Pod, container, and runtime readiness (not answerable)
panels.description: The kubelet sees the probes the chart renders, and the result reaches no series. llama-server's health endpoint is a probe target, not a metric. Scrape reachability, in the first row, is a different question.
panels.wouldRequire: kube-state-metrics for pod phase and container readiness, and an instrumented serving-runtime adapter for runtime readiness

panels.title: Requests finished since the API processes started
panels.description: Every request the API finished, every outcome, since each API process that is publishing now started, summed across replicas. A count rather than a rate, so the first request of a process is counted; the per-second view is the timeseries beside it.
panels.whenMissing: Missing: no API process is publishing its identity right now, so there is nothing to count against. See the collection row. This is not a zero.
panels.zeroMeans: An API process is publishing its identity right now, and no publishing API process has finished a request since it started.

panels.title: Requests per second, by workload, model, and outcome
panels.description: Outcome is one of success, client-error, server-error, and timeout. Summed across replicas on purpose: the question is about a workload, not a pod. A labelled counter series is created by its first event and first appears at whatever it has counted by its first scrape, at least 1. A rate needs two samples in its window and assumes no zero at creation, so it never sees those events, and for one scrape interval the new series has no row at all. Ten server-error outcomes before a first scrape have been observed reading 0 per second here. A series that exists and has not moved draws a flat 0 rather than this panel's missing text.
panels.whenMissing: Missing: no request has been finished since the API process started, so no series exists, or no API target is scraped. The since-start count separates the two.

panels.title: Requests in flight at the API, per replica
panels.description: Requests each API replica has accepted and not yet answered. instance is the pod name and the one unbounded label this dashboard shows; this panel is what it is paid for.
panels.whenMissing: Missing: no API replica has had a request since it started, or no API target is scraped. The in-flight series is created by a replica's first request; after that a replica with nothing in flight reads 0 and is present.

queries.expr: sum by (k8s_namespace, k8s_component, instance, inferops_workload_id, inferops_model_id) (inferops_inference_requests_in_flight)

panels.title: Serving runtime: requests processing and deferred
panels.description: The runtime's own view, through the chart's recording rules. It counts slots, not the API's accepted requests, and is not expected to match the API panel. Deferred says queueing happened and never how long anything waited. Read through a scrape and a recording rule, so a short burst can finish before either panel moves.
panels.whenMissing: Missing: the serving-runtime job discovered nothing, no collector is evaluating the recording rules, or this is the mock profile, which runs no serving runtime.

panels.title: Request duration P50, P95, and P99
panels.description: Quantiles of inferops_inference_request_duration_seconds, with bucket counters summed across replicas before the quantile is taken. A quantile is interpolated inside a bucket, so its resolution is the catalog's bucket boundaries. An operating figure, not a benchmark. Once the bucket series exist, a five-minute window with no request makes every quantile NaN, which draws as a gap in a line that is still present -- not as this panel's missing text. Every outcome is in the histogram, and a refused request is fast: a window holding mostly refusals reads lower here, whatever caused them. A wide bucket makes the interpolation coarse: a quantile can sit most of a bucket width away from what clients observed, so read it as a bucket, not a figure.
panels.whenMissing: Missing: no request has been finished since the API process started, so no bucket series exists, or no API target is scraped. An idle window after that shows gaps instead.

panels.title: Successful requests per second, by model
panels.description: Request throughput: requests that finished with outcome success. Token throughput is in the token row. A labelled counter series is created by its first event and first appears at whatever it has counted by its first scrape, at least 1. A rate needs two samples in its window and assumes no zero at creation, so it never sees those events, and for one scrape interval the new series has no row at all. A series that exists and has not moved draws a flat 0 rather than this panel's missing text.
panels.whenMissing: Missing: no request has succeeded since the API process started, so no series exists, or no API target is scraped. The requests count separates the two.

panels.title: Queue wait P95 (not emitted)
panels.description: How long a request waits before the runtime starts on it. The deferred count in the traffic row is the partial substitute: it shows that queueing happened and never for how long.
panels.whenMissing: Not emitted: inferops_inference_queue_duration_seconds is the serving-runtime adapter's measurement, and the adapter is not instrumented.

panels.title: Errors counted since the API processes started
panels.description: Every canonical error the API counted since each API process that is publishing now started, summed across replicas. A count rather than a rate, so a first error is never read as none.
panels.whenMissing: Missing: no API process is publishing its identity right now, so there is nothing to count against. See the collection row. This is not a zero.
panels.zeroMeans: An API process is publishing its identity right now, and no publishing API process has counted an error since it started.

panels.title: Share of requests that did not succeed, since the API processes started
panels.description: Requests with an outcome other than success, over all requests, counted since each publishing API process started. Cumulative for the same reason as the counts: a rate would miss the first failure of a new outcome.
panels.whenMissing: Missing: no request has been finished since the API processes started, and a share of no traffic is undefined rather than zero, or no API target is scraped. The requests count shows which.
panels.zeroMeans: Requests have been finished since the API processes started and every one of them succeeded. This zero rests on requests having been counted, not on an identity being published.

panels.title: Errors per second, by workload and canonical code
panels.description: inferops_error_code is the platform's canonical code, never an HTTP status and never a provider's message; the collector drops an HTTP status label on the way in. A labelled counter series is created by its first event and first appears at whatever it has counted by its first scrape, at least 1. A rate needs two samples in its window and assumes no zero at creation, so it never sees those events, and for one scrape interval the new series has no row at all. Ten capability-unavailable errors before a first scrape have been observed reading 0 per second here. A series that exists and has not moved draws a flat 0 rather than this panel's missing text.
panels.whenMissing: Missing: no error has been counted since the API process started, so no series exists, or no API target is scraped. The since-start count separates the two.

panels.title: Model load duration P95 (not emitted)
panels.description: The load durations this project has are stopwatch figures in evidence records, not series.
panels.whenMissing: Not emitted: inferops_model_load_duration_seconds is assigned to the serving-runtime adapter, which is not instrumented, and llama-server publishes no load duration either.

panels.title: API processes publishing an identity
panels.description: The recovery signal the API tier emits: a lost pod's identity series stops being returned once its target is marked stale, and its replacement publishes a new one under a new instance in the identity table. It counts processes the collector has read, not desired replicas, and it can lag a deletion by the discovery and scrape interval.
panels.whenMissing: Missing: no API process published an identity. This is not a zero.

panels.title: Restarts and pod phase (not answerable)
panels.description: The recovery run asked for kube_pod_container_status_restarts_total and received no series. A restart is visible here only indirectly, as an identity replaced under a new instance.

panels.title: API process CPU, per replica
panels.description: CPU seconds per second from the API process's own counter. It is the process, not the container: a cgroup limit, throttling, and working set are all elsewhere and none has a source.
panels.whenMissing: Missing: no API target is scraped.

panels.title: API process memory (not emitted)
panels.description: The catalog declares inferops_process_resident_memory_bytes, assigns it to the API, and marks it not emitted.
panels.whenMissing: Not emitted: the only per-process memory figure the standard library exposes is a file, and a module under src/inferops may not read one.

panels.title: Container and pod CPU and memory (not answerable)
panels.description: Neither the serving runtime's consumption nor any container's use against its declared request and limit reaches a series in the accepted cluster.
panels.wouldRequire: a kubelet cAdvisor scrape job, metrics-server, or kube-state-metrics, each a cluster add-on this chart does not own

panels.title: Scrape targets discovered, by tier
panels.description: Pods with a metrics port the collector found in each tier. The nearest thing to a replica count this telemetry has, and not the same thing: it is neither the desired count nor the ready count, and during a replacement it has been observed to include the pod being removed.
panels.whenMissing: Missing: no collector is evaluating this release's recording rules, or neither job has ever discovered a pod.

panels.title: Build, model, and runtime identity, per API replica
panels.description: One row per API process: service version, capability, release, environment, adapter kind, model and revision, runtime and image digest. inferops_adapter_kind reads mock or real, so a mock result stays visibly a mock. The chart's default leaves service_version empty, and an empty label value is shown as absent.
panels.whenMissing: Missing: no API process published an identity. The collection row says whether a target answered without one.

panels.title: Serving runtime operating identity
panels.description: The environment, workload, model, and runtime the collector attaches to the runtime's series, and how many runtime processes carry them. The immutable identity -- revision, image digest -- is not reachable from a runtime series, because a runtime series cannot be joined to the API's identity series.
panels.whenMissing: Missing: the serving-runtime job discovered nothing, no collector is evaluating the recording rules, or this is the mock profile, which runs no serving runtime.

panels.title: Cluster provider (not answerable)
panels.description: No telemetry attribute names the Kubernetes provider a release runs on. The provider is recorded in each evidence record, where the run that produced it was verified, and nowhere in a series.
panels.wouldRequire: a provider attribute in the telemetry catalog with a permitted metric or identity placement, and an emitter that sets it from the verified target rather than from configuration

panels.title: Tokens per second at the API, by model and direction
panels.description: Input and output tokens as the API counts them, at the API's boundary. A labelled counter series is created by its first event and first appears at whatever it has counted by its first scrape, at least 1. A rate needs two samples in its window and assumes no zero at creation, so it never sees those events, and for one scrape interval the new series has no row at all. A series that exists and has not moved draws a flat 0 rather than this panel's missing text.
panels.whenMissing: Missing: no completion has been counted since the API process started, or no API target is scraped.

panels.title: Tokens per second at the serving runtime, by model and direction
panels.description: The runtime's own counters, mapped by the chart's recording rules. A different measurement from the API's, and not expected to match it. Input excludes prompt tokens llama-server served from its prompt cache, so input here is not the API's input; output has been observed to match the API exactly. Read through a scrape and a recording rule, so it can trail the API by a minute.
panels.whenMissing: Missing: the serving-runtime job discovered nothing, no collector is evaluating the recording rules, or this is the mock profile, which runs no serving runtime.

notPanelled.reason: Deferred out of V1 by the catalog. There is no streaming path, so a panel would show request duration a second time under another name.
Deferred out of V1 by the catalog. There is no retry path, and a panel that can only read zero reads as a healthy system rather than an absent feature.
Deferred out of V1 by the catalog. No platform component computes or emits a cost record.
Its emitter is the contract validator, a library and a command rather than a running service, so there is no endpoint to scrape.

limitations.statement: The generated JSON has been imported into one Grafana, 11.6.0, through file provisioning, and rendered in a headless browser at one viewport. It has not been checked against Grafana's own schema validation or any other version. In that rendering a stat panel's missing text longer than about a line shrinks until it cannot be read: the panel still draws no number, and its title still says what it counts, but the explanation is illegible.

Eleven panel expressions are new in this record. Beyond the fixture evaluator, one real Prometheus has evaluated them: the collector of one single-replica release on docker-desktop, in nine states. Nothing has evaluated them on kind or with two replicas.

A since-start count fills its zero while any API process publishes inferops_build_info, and a share fills its zero where any request was counted. Neither is per replica: with two replicas and one of them not publishing, the figure is the publishing replica's alone and still reads as a number. The share does not depend on identity at all, so it reads 0 beside an API that publishes none. And a since-start count starts again when a process restarts. The collection row is what shows each gap. Nothing checks what a zero fill is keyed to: the rule only requires that a panel filling one says what its zero means.
Totals sum every series in the selected store. A store holding two releases would add them together.
Scrape reachability and the identity count follow discovery and scrape timing, and a deleted pod has been observed reading up for fifteen seconds. Neither is a timely failure signal.

Every rate panel inherits two properties of a real Prometheus that the fixture evaluator does not model, and both were observed. A labelled counter series first appears at whatever it counted before its first scrape, so a rate never counts those events: ten refused requests read 0 per second while the since-start count rose by ten. And after a target stops answering, a rate over a five-minute window keeps returning the pre-outage figure: with no API process running, the request rate still read a success rate, while the since-start counts were empty. Those counts vanish at once when a target fails its scrape, but a deleted pod's series linger until they go stale.
Profiles decide which queries the fixture evaluator runs. The Grafana JSON sends every query whatever the release's profile, and a real-only query against a mock release returns an empty result.

Until a deleted API pod's series go stale, a since-start count sums the dead process and its replacement, and the identity count reads one more process than is running. Once they go stale, every since-start count starts again from 0, which says nothing about errors a minute earlier.

The runtime's input token counter counts prompt tokens llama-server evaluated, not those it served from its prompt cache, so the two token panels disagree on input and cannot be compared. How far apart they are depends on prompt reuse. Output tokens matched exactly in the one run that compared them, which reused a single prompt.
